## Findings

1. **Rewrite fixes follow-ups.** Across the 17 follow-up cases, hit@1 goes from 0.53 (naive) to 0.65 and MRR from 0.68 to 0.79; overall hit@3 goes from 0.83 to 0.97. Corrections gain the most (hit@1 0.50 → 1.00), and small talk is detected in 3/3 cases, where naive search returns articles for "Thanks, that's all!".
2. **Pasting the history in is not a substitute.** Config 2 (full history) is no better than naive overall (hit@1 0.60 vs 0.63) and scores 0.00 on corrections, because the superseded topic is still in the query. It only wins on multi-reference questions.
3. **BM25 fixes exact codes.** Adding BM25 (config 3 → 4) lifts `exact_code` hit@1 from 0.80 to 1.00 (vector search ranks SS-110 above SS-111) and overall hit@1 from 0.70 to 0.80. Keyword search alone misses two of four paraphrases entirely, so the two retrievers cover each other's gaps.
4. **Reranking helps the top 3 but not the top 1 here.** Config 5 raises hit@3 from 0.93 to 0.97 and fixes paraphrases (0.75 → 1.00) and corrections (0.75 → 1.00), but hit@1 drops from 0.80 to 0.77 and MRR from 0.870 to 0.864. Three cases regress (C-004, C-007, C-014).
5. **Why reranking regresses: over-specified rewrites.** The rewriter tends to add the store name and the full product name plus SKU. The cross-encoder then scores a chunk that repeats those words above the policy chunk that answers the question. Measured directly: "Do gift cards expire?" scores the gift-card expiry chunk at 0.999, while the actual rewrite "Do Northwind Gear digital gift cards expire?" scores it at 0.05, below the warranty overview (0.35). The same effect makes `pronoun` hit@1 fall after rewriting (0.60 → 0.20–0.40), although the expected article stays in the top 3 for all five pronoun cases.
6. **One genuine rewrite error.** In C-016 "the second one" was resolved to PayPal instead of the installment plan. History has no speaker labels, so "second" is ambiguous between the second message and the second topic.
7. **Latency.** Naive search takes about 0.1 s. The rewrite adds about 0.7 s on average (p95 1.7 s). Reranking 10 candidates adds about 2.5 s on this machine (12th Gen Intel i5-12450H laptop, roughly 0.3 s per 90-token pair), so the full pipeline averages 3.3 s with p95 4.7 s. With `RERANK_CANDIDATES=5` the full pipeline measures p95 2.85 s, at a cost in quality (hit@1 0.73, hit@3 0.93, MRR 0.822).
8. **Cost.** The benchmark made 22 Claude calls on its first run (one per eval case with history) and 0 on every re-run. No rewrite fell back.

| Rerank (5) improves hit@1 or MRR over config 4 | **Not met**: hit@1 0.77 vs 0.80, MRR 0.864 vs 0.870 (hit@3 improves, 0.93 → 0.97). Cause in finding 5 |
| Full pipeline p95 latency < 3 s on CPU | **Not met** at the default `RERANK_CANDIDATES=10`: p95 4.7 s on this laptop. 2.85 s at `RERANK_CANDIDATES=5`, with lower quality (finding 7) |
| Total real Anthropic calls ≤ 50 for the whole build | Met: 33 |
| All quality gates green | Met |

## What was not done, and why

- **Prompt v2.** The fix for finding 5 is a prompt change: tell the rewriter not to add the store name, and to keep the product name only when the question is about the product itself. `PROMPT_VERSION` is part of the cache key, so this re-runs all 22 rewrites. With 33 of 50 calls already used, that does not fit under the hard cap, so the prompt was left at v1.
- **Tuning.** `RERANK_CANDIDATES` 20 and 30 were tried from cache (zero API calls) and gave identical quality to 10, so the default was kept. No other parameter was tuned.
- **Faster reranking.** Int8 quantization or an ONNX backend for the cross-encoder would cut the rerank time; neither was implemented.
- **Sample size.** 30 retrieval cases: one case is 0.03 of hit@1, so the 0.80 vs 0.77 difference between configs 4 and 5 is a single case.
